question: What is the canonical definition of 'locatable elements' for SPIDER fragment yield — derived from Method1's 150-element shopping estimate — and does yield_locatable stabilize across randomized shopping page types (including checkout) under that frozen definition?
hypothesis: Method1's 150-element shopping estimate can be traced to a specific element-counting method in the derivation code (analysis_output.json from EXP-INTEL-33945226776). That method defines a canonical 'locatable element' for SPIDER. Under this frozen definition, yield_locatable = viewport_elements / locatable_elements will be approximately 0.365 (within 10pp) across randomized shopping page types (product-listing, detail, cart, checkout), confirming the fragment model captures ~36% of locatable elements and the 812-task corpus is viable for C-CROSSSITE evaluation.
falsifier: The forensic analysis cannot trace Method1's 150-element estimate to a specific counting method (definition remains ambiguous after code inspection), OR yield_locatable under the frozen definition has CV > 0.2 across 8+ randomized shopping tasks (yield unstable across page types), OR yield_locatable mean differs from Method1 0.365 by >15pp under the frozen definition (method mismatch), OR checkout page type shows yield systematically different from other page types (>20pp delta on >50% of checkout tasks).
baselines: Method1 estimate from EXP-INTEL-33945226776: shopping yield 0.365 (element-count method, 150 elements per product_listing)
Heuristic estimate from EXP-INTEL-33945226776: shopping yield 0.65 (FALSIFIED under all denominators in EXP-INTEL-34546944360, confirmed robust)
Parent pilot N=2 from EXP-INTEL-34377576886: yield_cdp = 0.0427, yield_locatable = 0.38 (parent 258 definition)

Parent N=20 from EXP-INTEL-34546944360: yield_cdp = 0.0426 (CDP stable), yield_locatable = 0.079 (Definition 1: all-elements-with-bbox), ~0.32 (Definition 2: interactive-only), ~0.42 (Definition 3: parent 258)
Yield_cdp 0.0426 (stable across 20 tasks, CV=0.12) as cross-denominator floor
positive_control: The frozen measurement script produces non-empty viewport_elements (>0) and locatable_elements (>viewport_elements) on all tasks. Forensic analysis of Method1 derivation code produces a traceable element-counting method that maps to one of the three candidate definitions (all-elements-with-bbox, interactive-only, or parent CSS selectors).
null_control: If the forensic analysis cannot resolve the definition (all three candidate definitions remain equally plausible after code inspection), the experiment reports MIXED with 'definition_ambiguous' status. This is a valid negative outcome: the denominator cannot be resolved, and the 812-task corpus is unreliable for yield claims.
measurement_validity: Docker Hub am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping:latest is pullable and accessible at localhost:8080 (verified in parent EXP-INTEL-34546944360)
Frozen measurement script with sha256 recorded; script implements frozen definition from forensic analysis
Fresh browser context per task (no shared context between tasks)
Raw accessibility tree saved for each task (initial viewport only — scroll not required for denominator resolution) with durable sha256
Task selection randomized from WebArena-Verified dataset covering product-listing, detail, cart, and checkout page types
Docker image digest recorded before measurement to bound drift
Method1 derivation code (analysis_output.json from EXP-INTEL-33945226776) available for forensic inspection
Per-task viewport element sample saved (not just aggregate) to investigate constant viewport 108 anomaly
Both yield_cdp and yield_locatable reported for every task with explicit denominator definition in metrics
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) forensic analysis traces Method1 150-element estimate to a specific counting method (definition resolved), AND (2) yield_locatable under frozen definition has CV < 0.2 across all measured shopping tasks (yield stable), AND (3) yield_locatable mean is within 15pp of Method1 0.365 (method compatible), THEN verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for denominator resolution and C-CROSSSITE corpus viability. If forensic analysis resolves definition BUT yield is unstable (CV > 0.2) or far from Method1 (>15pp), verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (definition resolved but yield not workable). If forensic analysis cannot resolve definition, verdict = MIXED with 'definition_ambiguous' status (denominator cannot be resolved, corpus unreliable). GitLab/Reddit comparison: if infrastructure available, yield must be within 2x of shopping yield to support C-CROSSSITE; if BLOCKED, mark with infrastructure proof and note as unresolved for C-CROSSSITE generalization.
product_consequence_positive: Resolving the denominator unblocks the 812-task corpus for C-CROSSSITE/C-LLM-INHERIT evaluation. If the frozen definition yields ~36% fragment yield, the observation pipeline captures sufficient interactive elements for fragment reuse. Product lane can proceed to integration experiments with the 812-task corpus. The canonical definition also enables consistent yield measurement across future experiments.
product_consequence_negative: If the forensic analysis cannot resolve the definition, the 812-task corpus cannot be reliably used for yield claims. Product lane must either (a) redesign the observation pipeline to capture a definable set of elements, (b) use CDP yield (4%) as the conservative floor and accept that fragment model captures minimal content, or (c) explore alternative corpora where element counting is unambiguous. The denominator ambiguity would be confirmed as a structural property of the fragment model, not a solvable measurement problem.
estimated_cost: Medium: Docker container management, Playwright automation across 8-10 tasks, forensic code analysis, raw artifact preservation. Estimated 2-3 hours of compute time. Forensic analysis adds ~30 minutes of code inspection.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the single blocking question for the 812-task corpus viability. A clear denominator resolution (either resolved and workable, or resolved and not workable, or confirmed ambiguous) changes the product decision from UNKNOWN to a actionable state. Even a MIXED outcome (definition ambiguous by construction) is valuable because it closes the denominator question and forces a product redesign decision.
